newsitem.title: KENYA: Former Katanga gendarmes offer to fight for Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Former Katanga gendarmes offer to fight for Zaire.

text.p: A leader of former Katangan gendarmes, veterans of military campaigns against Zairean President Mobutu Seko Sese, offered on Monday to fight alongside Mobutu's troops against rebel and Rwandan forces in the east.

In a statement sent from Lubumbashi, Zaire, Colonel Songolo Nura called on the Zaire government to arm the former gendarmes and give them logistical support "so that we can go to the front to defend our territory invaded by foreign Rwandese troops".

Tutsi-led rebels have captured a string of towns in eastern Zaire and correspondents have given eyewitness accounts of Rwanda's troops entering the Zairean city of Goma to fight against Mobutu's forces.

The former Katangan gendarmes, now grouped in the Zaire National Liberation Front (FLNC), fought two military campaigns against Mobutu in the late 1970s. Moroccan troops helped to put down the first rebellion, while French and Belgian soldiers quelled the second.
In 1990, when Mobutu recognized the FLNC as part of Zaire's moves towards a multi-party system, the gendarmes laid down their arms.
Though currently disarmed, the FLNC is considered a potentially significant force in the mineral-rich province of Shaba, as Katanga is now called, African analysts said.
In his statement, Nura strongly condemned proposed South African arms sales to Rwanda.

On Monday South Africa said it would scrap the sales if asked to do so by leaders of central Africa's "Great Lakes" region. Many of those leaders will meet at an African summit in Nairobi on Tuesday dealing with the conflict in eastern Zaire.
